CheckTitle: Worker scripts should not store secrets as plain-text environment variables
Description: Checks that Cloudflare Worker scripts do not use plain-text environment variable bindings to store sensitive values such as API keys, tokens, or passwords. These should use Secret bindings which are encrypted and not exposed in the dashboard.
Risk: Plain-text env vars are visible to all dashboard users and are not encrypted at rest. A compromised Cloudflare account or insider threat can directly read these values, potentially exposing downstream services.

Code.Other: In the Cloudflare dashboard: Worker > Settings > Variables and Secrets > Add Secret

Recommendation.Text: Move any sensitive values from plain-text environment variables to Secret bindings. Secrets are encrypted at rest and not visible in the dashboard after creation.

Notes: Variable names matching patterns like 'secret', 'token', 'key', 'password', 'api_key', 'auth', 'credential', 'webhook' are flagged as likely secrets.
